item.title: 5 people found alive after 3 months adrift at sea in tiny 20-foot boat
item.description: After drifting for three months across the Pacific Ocean from Micronesia, five survivors, including two children, were found off Fanning Island in Kiribati.
item.content:encoded:
Five people, including two children, have been rescued in the remote Pacific Ocean after surviving for three months adrift in a small boat, according to authorities and international news outlets.  

The three adults and two children who were rescued on Nov. 1 were among nine passengers in total who set out July 30. Their trip was intended to be a routine, one-hour crossing between the Micronesian islands of Murilo and Ruo, according to reports from the Australian Broadcasting Corp. (ABC) and The Times of London.

Shortly after departure, however, a sudden storm pushed the 20-foot skiff off course, leaving it stranded in open waters.

CRUISE SHIP BATTLES ROUGH PACIFIC SEAS TO SAVE INJURED, STRANDED SAILOR

Following the disappearance, the U.S. Coast Guard launched an extensive search operation across the region.

After scouring over 25,000 nautical miles across 31 search patterns without locating the vessel, the agency suspended its active search on Aug. 10, it said in an initial news release.

The ordeal ended when residents of Fanning Island in Kiribati spotted the vessel drifting off their coast and brought the five passengers ashore, according to the ABC and The Times.

Kiribati lawmaker Kaotitaake Rakoroa told news outlets the survivors were taken in by a local church pastor, who provided immediate shelter and care. 

The five were suffering from severe malnutrition and dehydration upon arrival.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Despite their physical condition, local medical staff noted steady improvement.

Paukin Tororo, a nursing officer treating the survivors, told the ABC that the group had started showing positive signs of recovery, including smiling, moving their heads and indicating an appetite for food.

Authorities have not released details on how the group survived the three-month journey or what happened to the four passengers who remain unaccounted for to this day.

"Incredible and wonderful news. These five folks were found and are receiving care," the U.S. Coast Guard told The Associated Press (AP) in an email.

"Our profound condolences to family and friends of those who did not arrive with them," the message also said. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

When asked by the AP what happened to the missing four, the Coast Guard said it was continuing to gather and confirm information and would reply as soon as possible.

Alexander Narruhn, governor of Micronesia’s Chuuk state, has started discussions with the Kiribati government to arrange repatriation for the survivors, the AP said.

"There were nine people aboard the boat that went missing. Thanks be to God for his love and mercy that five of the nine have been found," Narruhn said through an interpreter in a statement cited by the AP.

"We continue to pray for their four companions."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The members of the group are yet to speak publicly about their ordeal and have asked for their privacy to be respected. 

Family members in the Federated States of Micronesia told media outlets they have been in contact with some of the group.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Coast Guard for further comment and details.

item.title: Charles Barkley has heartfelt Veterans Day message interrupted on air by an untimely phone call
item.description: Charles Barkley's passionate Veterans Day message on "Inside the NBA" was interrupted when Kenny Smith's phone went off loud enough to announce the caller.
item.content:encoded:
Charles Barkley tried delivering a serious and important message about Veterans Day during Wednesday's edition of "Inside The NBA" on ESPN. The keyword there is "tried."

During the opening segment of the show, Barkley spoke about how his father served the United States and went on to work for Veterans Affairs before explaining that more needs to be done for our veterans.

"I've always said this. We talk a good game, but we don’t do nearly enough for our veterans," Barkley shared. "Our government has to do better. Number one, we should always show them love, but our government has to do better for our veterans. If you give your body, a lot of people have passed away, some of these other guys are injured, and obviously there is the mental strain that none of us..."

CHARLES BARKLEY CALLS OUT LEBRON JAMES FOR DISRESPECTING THE NATIONAL ANTHEM WITH PRACTICE GOLF SWING

It was at this moment that Barkley was cut off, but not from one of his co-hosts saying something in agreement or anything of that nature, but by a cell phone sitting next to him going off.

The phone belonged to co-host Kenny Smith, and to say he had his phone on loud would be an understatement. The phone was so loud, in fact, you could hear the phone say the name of the person ringing him.

Like the consummate professional that he is, Barkley got right back to delivering his passionate message about veterans around the country.

"The mental strain that these guys are under once you are in the service, so we need to do better with our service members, plain and simple," Barkley concluded.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This won't be added to the endless list of great moments that Barkley, Johnson and Smith have been a part of sharing a desk together, but it's certainly a unique one.

Last month, Johnson announced that he will be stepping away from "Inside The NBA" at the conclusion of the season. The 70-year-old shared that he had undergone bypass surgery 14 months ago, explaining that he wants to slow down and spend more time with his wife and five grandchildren.

Barkley, who has sat alongside Johnson on the show since 2000, told WSFA News in September that this too will be his last NBA season working on TV.

item.title: Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman explains the meaning of his meme-worthy side-eye
item.description: Marcus Freeman's viral side eye during Notre Dame's win over the Miami Hurricanes became an instant meme, and his players know the look well.
item.content:encoded:
It seems like on an almost weekly basis, a new meme is born somewhere in the world of sports, and one of the most recent came to us courtesy of Notre Dame head football coach Marcus Freeman.

The moment happened during the Fighting Irish's 31-24 win over the Miami Hurricanes, and it quickly became the internet's favorite meme du jour.

Freeman was getting an explanation from officials, and pretty clearly wasn't liking what they were saying.

I felt that look, and I wasn't even involved.

It turns out that Freeman's side-eye is a familiar look to his players, and he discussed it alongside Notre Dame safety Luke Talich on the program's "Wake Up the Echoes."

49ERS COACH KYLE SHANAHAN EXPLAINS VIRAL SIDELINE EXCHANGE WITH BROCK PURDY, WHO YELLED AT HIM DURING GAME

"That's the definition of, 'You're tripping,'" Freeman said when asked about the look. "There's some other descriptions I can give, but I'm not going to say it on here."

I think we can all make some assumptions as to what those might be.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Freeman also said that Talich has been on the receiving end of that side-eyed glare.

"It's usually on special teams," Talich admitted.

NICK SABAN TELLS THEO VON HIS FAMOUS SIDELINE INTENSITY WAS A CALCULATED STRATEGY, NOT EMOTION

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He was then asked what goes through his head when his coach fires off that meme-worthy look, and it turns out, it does a pretty good job of communicating its intent.

"Well, I usually know why I'm getting the side eye," he continued. "So I kind of know what I got to do. But yeah, as you said, I'm tripping."

Aren't we all tripping sometimes?

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Well, you probably would be tripping way less frequently if you knew that one slip-up (trip-up?) could mean getting cooked with one of the nastiest side-eyes I've ever seen since I refused to give my French Bulldog a chunk of pizza crust.

I think he still resents me for that.

item.title: UN renews Iran's committee seat amid war with US, sparking backlash: 'Morally bankrupt'
item.description: The United Nations reconfirmed Iran to a key committee with 144 votes, drawing fierce opposition from Canada, Australia and U.S. lawmakers.
item.content:encoded:
The United Nations reconfirmed Iran to its seat on the Committee for Programme and Coordination on Wednesday, sparking outrage from member states who believe the country’s record of aggression should disqualify its representatives from the committee’s work to review human rights, women’s rights and counterterrorism programs.

Ahead of the vote, Hillel Neuer, executive director of UN Watch, a human rights watchdog, said he believes the move gives Iran another tool for the regime’s propaganda machine.

"They use it," Neuer said. "You'll see a headline in Iranian propaganda right away: ‘Hey, look, we were elected to yet another body.' And it sends a signal… As they're killing their own people, what does the world have to say?"

Neuer believes Iran’s continued spot on the committee gives Tehran a nod of international legitimacy amid its ongoing conflict with the U.S., showcasing the U.N.’s uneven record for creating a forum to deter international violence.

ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES

"Sometimes [the U.N.] is effective. Sometimes they’re not. Sometimes, even when they’re effective, they’re effective in a bad way. There’s an effect, but it’s to empower dictatorships," Neuer said.

"The U.N. spends a lot of its time attacking democracies like America, like Israel. America gets condemned every year for the embargo in Cuba. Last year, there was one resolution on Iran, one on North Korea, one on Myanmar — and 15 on Israel. And Hamas, Islam and jihad were never mentioned once. That happens a lot at the U.N."

Iran was reconfirmed with the support of 144 ballots cast by the U.N. General Assembly.

The Committee for Programme and Coordination consists of 34 member states, each of which is elected to the body for a three-year term. Although it is not one of the U.N.’s six main committees, it reviews the organization’s plans and priorities, making recommendations on their design, priorities, coordination and effectiveness.

Iran’s renewal to the post prompted an outcry from lawmakers in the U.S. on Tuesday afternoon.

"The United Nations elected Iran — the world’s biggest exporter of terrorism — to the committee responsible for establishing priorities on disarmament, counterterrorism and women’s rights," the House Foreign Affairs Committee wrote in a statement posted to X.

FREED AMERICAN REVEALS BRUTAL IRAN PRISON ORDEAL, WARNS HOSTAGES FACE GREATER DANGER

"The United Nations is morally bankrupt: no sane person can take it seriously."

Similarly, Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand issued her own statement condemning the move.

"Canada is steadfastly opposed to giving Iran a seat on the UN Committee for Programme and Coordination — and Canada voted against Iran’s inclusion today at the UN. The committee should be comprised of countries entrusted with shaping the work of the United Nations and must uphold the principles of its Charter. The Iranian regime silences dissent at home and fuels instability across the Middle East. We stand with the people of Iran," Anand said.

Notably, Australia also joined the opposition, voting alongside Canada against Iran’s confirmation.

"Australia strongly opposes Iran’s nomination to the UN Committee for Programme and Coordination and voted against. Iran’s human rights violations and destabilizing conduct undermine multilateralism," Foreign Minister Penny Wong wrote.

Neuer believes it's not just Western countries that will be watching how the U.N. treats Iran. He noted that aggressors constantly monitor the international field to get a sense of how it might react in the future.

"It's like Putin looks when Obama said we 'have a red line in Syria. Use chemical weapons — red line.' Well, Syria used chemical weapons. And Obama... did nothing. That sent a message. Shortly thereafter, Putin invaded Ukraine. I'm not saying that invasions are gonna happen the next day, but these things send messages, and constantly governments are taking the temperature. What is the pushback?" Neuer said.

He also observed that although many in the U.S. view the U.N. with some skepticism, other countries still use the group as a barometer of international consensus.

"The United Nations is considered for many a repository of international legitimacy; it may not be so in the United States… but in many parts of the world it is regarded as the arbiter of international legitimacy," Neuer said.

IRAN IS NOT A NORMAL NATION YOU CAN MAKE DEALS WITH; IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT

"What is the signal you're giving to the ayatollah regime? They murdered tens of thousands of people. They're hanging dissidents. They are torturing women who defend their right not to cover every piece of their hair. They beat political prisoners. What message does the world have to send? Did you give them a pat on the back? Or did you? Did you penalize them?"

item.title: Matt Lambert, DC doctor, identified as gunman in deadly attack after HOA feud
item.description: Dr. Matt Lambert allegedly posted a manifesto referencing an engineering report minutes before the deadly Vida gym shooting in Logan Circle.
item.content:encoded:
The gunman involved in Thursday's deadly gym shooting in Washington, D.C., has been identified by law enforcement sources as Dr. Matt Lambert, who had an apparent dispute with his homeowner's association.

Lambert's identity was confirmed by a pair of law enforcement officials and a source familiar with the matter who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity.

Authorities said the shooter opened fire around 8 a.m. inside Vida gym in D.C.'s Logan Circle neighborhood. One person was killed, and four others were wounded. The gunman was also killed.

DC GYM SHOOTING KILLS 1, INJURES 4; GUNMAN DEAD, SOURCES SAY

According to a report from The Associated Press, the shooter had an ongoing issue with building management at his apartment building and filed a lawsuit against the company last year.

LISTEN: DC shooting dispatch audio reveals 30 people sheltered in gym basement as gunfire erupted

Less than 10 minutes before the first calls about the gunfire came in, according to the AP, Lambert appeared to post "My manifesto is an engineering report" on an X account named "OfMiceandMold" with screenshots from that report.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The photos show the dispute between Lambert and the Metropole Condominium Association over problems like "mold" and "water intrusion" issues.

SEND US A TIP

The account features numerous posts, photos and videos of alleged issues inside the apartment. In a post from the beginning of October, he called out his HOA for what he said were "months of 'Luigi' tactics" and mentioned submitting "an independent engineering report."

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

The shooting is still under investigation.

item.title: Hospital sewers may be breeding grounds for dangerous superbugs, study finds
item.description: A Nature Communications study found hospital wastewater promotes antibiotic-resistant E. coli, with bacteria on sewer pipes three times as resistant.
item.content:encoded:
Hospital wastewater has been shown to promote the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, potentially making sewer systems hotspots for antimicrobial resistance, according to a new Swedish study published in Nature Communications.

Antibiotics taken by patients can pass through their bodies and enter hospital sewer systems, creating conditions that favor the growth of resistant bacteria.

Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria develop the ability to survive drugs designed to kill them, making some infections harder to treat. More than 9.3 million drug-resistant infections occur in the U.S. each year, resulting in more than 39,000 deaths, according to the CDC's 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report.

DANGEROUS DRUG-RESISTANT FUNGUS SPREADS ACROSS US, REACHING 27 STATES

The researchers conducted a study involving wastewater from 10 hospitals and eight municipal wastewater treatment plants.

They wanted to determine whether hospital wastewater actually promoted the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, rather than simply carrying resistant bacteria from patients.

First, the researchers filtered hospital wastewater to remove existing bacteria, then exposed other bacteria to the filtered water in laboratory experiments. All 10 hospital samples significantly favored the growth of E. coli strains resistant to ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime, two antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections.

None of the eight municipal wastewater samples showed the same effect.

DEATH REPORTED IN E COLI OUTBREAK LINKED TO CALIFORNIA PUMPKIN PATCH AS MORE CASES EMERGE

This suggested that something in the wastewater itself was helping antibiotic-resistant bacteria thrive, according to the researchers.

The team also placed plastic plates in sewer pipes to study bacteria growing on their surfaces. After 30 days, bacteria growing on surfaces inside the pipes were about three times as likely to be resistant to the two antibiotics as bacteria in the surrounding wastewater. This pattern was not observed in municipal sewers.

The researchers also measured antibiotic levels in the wastewater and tested whether those same concentrations helped resistant bacteria grow in laboratory experiments. They found that ciprofloxacin was a major contributor, while cefotaxime also played a role.

BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE

"The discovery [suggests] that hospital sewers could be a spawning ground for bacteria that are difficult to treat with antibiotics," Joakim Larsson, professor of environmental pharmacology at the University of Gothenburg and Director of Centre for Antibiotic Resistance Research, told Fox News Digital.

"Knowing where resistant bacteria are promoted — and where they are less likely to be — is crucial when deciding how resources and efforts should be allocated to limit risks for antibiotic resistance development."

The study had several limitations. All sampling sites were in Sweden, and researchers focused primarily on E. coli and a limited number of antibiotics, so the findings may not apply to all bacteria or locations.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The sewer experiment lasted approximately 30 days, leaving longer-term effects unclear. The study also did not determine whether the growth of resistant bacteria in hospital sewers leads to more infections in patients or surrounding communities.

Although the study did not directly link hospital wastewater to human infections, Larsson said resistant bacteria could potentially reach people through contaminated water.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"When it rains heavily, treatment plants are typically overloaded, and release untreated or partially untreated wastewater with lots of bacteria," Larsson told Fox News Digital.

"If people get in contact with such waters, they can acquire those bacteria and then continue spreading them from person to person," he went on. "One thing that remains uncertain is how much you need to be exposed for resistant bacteria to colonize your gut or infect you."

The researchers identified two possible approaches to reducing antibiotic resistance in hospital sewers.

One involves using alternative antibiotics that are less likely to pass through patients' bodies unchanged and promote the growth of resistant bacteria in wastewater.

"But – and it is an important but – the patients’ need for antibiotics must not be compromised," Larsson said, emphasizing that equally effective alternatives may not always be available, and patients' medical needs must come first.

The second approach involves treating wastewater at hospitals to remove antibiotics that promote resistance, particularly fluoroquinolones and beta-lactams (two classes of antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections), while also removing harmful bacteria.

Larsson said treating wastewater at municipal plants would likely be less effective because antibiotic concentrations are high enough to favor resistant bacteria, primarily in hospital sewers.

Existing technologies can remove antibiotics from wastewater, but they can be costly and require additional treatment, he noted.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"When we know more about the drivers, we think it might be possible to develop technical solutions that are targeted and hopefully less expensive," Larsson added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the American Hospital Association requesting comment.

item.title: Pro kayak setups can cost $25K, but a national champion says beginners don't need to spend big
item.description: Three-time national champion Wyatt Hammond reveals why some pro kayak fishing setups now cost $25,000 and rival traditional bass fishing boats.
item.content:encoded:
When you think of kayak fishing, you probably picture somebody paddling around a lake in a little plastic boat, hoping to catch a few bass.

You probably don't picture a $25,000 fishing machine loaded with motors, electronics and enough gadgets to make a traditional bass boat jealous.

But that's exactly what some professional kayak anglers are using these days.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"I know there's a couple guys out here running $25,000 kayaks," three-time national champion Wyatt Hammond told OutKick OutDoors. "I always see everybody talking about it like, 'That looks like a spaceship compared to a kayak.'"

And while that might sound ridiculous to the average weekend fisherman, Hammond doesn't see anything particularly unusual about it.

"I just kind of equate it to the highest-end cars versus the cars that most people drive," he explained. "They look so far beyond what you'd imagine a car to look like. Or just even the bass boats that are running around with five or six depth finders on them.

"The highest-end boats versus the highest-end kayaks are pretty comparable."

Watch Wyatt Hammond's full interview with OutKick OutDoors here:

Hammond knows a thing or two about competitive kayak fishing. He won the 2025 Bassmaster Kayak Series National Championship, along with back-to-back Kayak Bass Fishing (KBF) National Championships in 2024 and 2025.

And last month, he came within just 2 inches of defending his Bassmaster title at Lake Murray in South Carolina.

But despite competing at the highest level of the sport, Hammond says one of the biggest reasons he chose kayak fishing over traditional bass boat tournaments was actually the cost.

He used to own a bass boat himself, but eventually decided the expenses weren't worth it.

"I ended up having to get rid of it because of the maintenance fees and all of that," he said. "Just putting gas in it all the time — a 36-gallon tank. It's, you know, $150 just to put gas in it, and then tires and all the maintenance things like that."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

His kayak, on the other hand, is a different story.

"I couldn't tell you the last time I put gas in my kayak," Hammond joked.

Of course, that doesn't mean his current setup is cheap. Hammond is a member of the Old Town pro team and fishes out of an AutoPilot 136, a motorized fishing kayak that can be outfitted with sophisticated electronics and plenty of other accessories.

But he insists you don't have to spend anywhere near $25,000 to get started.

Hammond admits he took what he calls the "expensive route" when he first got into kayak fishing.

"I went the very expensive route of buying a $200 kayak, and then a $400 kayak, and then a $700 kayak, and then a $2,000 kayak, and then a $5,000 kayak," he laughed.

Looking back, he says he would have been better off skipping a few of those upgrades and investing in a decent pedal-drive kayak from the beginning.

"I always kind of suggest going with, at the very least, a pedal-drive kayak if you want to get into the kayak fishing world, because that opens up your mobility around the lake, as well as it lets you be hands-free."

COOPER GALLANT SLEPT IN HIS TRUCK FOR YEARS CHASING PRO FISHING DREAM: 'I DIDN'T HAVE A PLAN B'

That means anglers can cast, change lures or work their electronics while continuing to move through the water.

And Hammond says a middle-of-the-road setup is more than enough to compete.

He even used one of his older kayaks at a national championship on Lake Guntersville in Alabama last year.

"I actually paddled that kayak," he said. "You don't need too, too much."

Beyond the price tag, Hammond says fishing from a kayak has actually made him a better angler.

Unlike competitors in high-powered bass boats, who can race miles across a lake in search of better fishing, kayak anglers have to be more deliberate about where they spend their time.

"You can't be kind of ADHD on a kayak, because you can't really up and just run 10 miles down the lake if you want to," he explained.

"So it kind of helps you as a fisherman as well. It helps you learn to break down water, and you're stuck in your little area, more or less. So you've got to figure out how all the fish are acting and make the best of the area that you choose."

And that's probably the most interesting thing about the rise of high-tech kayak fishing.

Sure, some competitors are spending enough money on their setups to buy a decent used car. But at its core, the sport still rewards anglers who know how to find fish and make the most of what's in front of them.

Whether they're fishing from a $25,000 spaceship or something a whole lot closer to the kayak sitting in your garage.

Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube!

item.title: Soldier who scolded Hegseth's entourage at Tomb of Unknown Soldier receives special honor from Pentagon chief
item.description: War Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal to the soldier who reprimanded his staff at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Thursday awarded a medal to the Army soldier who reprimanded him and his entourage at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier after laughter was heard from the group on Veterans Day.

"We love soldiers. We love standards," Hegseth wrote Thursday in a post on X. "Well done, Specialist."

"Carry on Patriots," he added.

A Pentagon official confirmed to Fox News Digital in a Thursday statement that Hegseth had "proudly" awarded Spc. Thomas Iglesias the medal for "the execution of his duties."

TRUMP DEFENDS PENTAGON CHIEF AS MASSIE TARGETS HIM: 'HEGSETH SHOULD BE PRAISED, NOT IMPEACHED'

"As shown in the photos, Secretary Hegseth welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard, to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," the official said.

The Joint Service Commendation Medal is awarded to members of the military who distinguish themselves through meritorious achievement or service, typically while serving in joint military operations or activities.

The award comes after video from Wednesday showed Iglesias reminding visitors to remain silent and maintain decorum after laughter was heard as Hegseth and his entourage walked away from the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier following a Veterans Day ceremony.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the soldier commanded to the entourage at the time.

TUNNEL TO TOWERS PAYS OFF MORTGAGES FOR 30 MILITARY FAMILIES IN VETERANS DAY TRIBUTE: 'A GREAT SACRIFICE'

Following the incident on Wednesday, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told CBS News that Hegseth and "the entire Department have always honored-and will always honor-the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe."

"While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell added.

item.title: Harry Kane An NFL Kicker? Patriots Star Drake Maye Supports It
item.description: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fully endorses Harry Kane’s dream of one day becoming an NFL kicker.
item.content:encoded:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fully endorses Harry Kane's dream of one day becoming an NFL kicker.

Maye spoke Thursday after practice at the campus of Bayern Munich — Kane's soccer team — ahead of Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions.

"It would be cool to see him try," Maye said. "He’s dealt with pressure, that's one of the biggest things about kicking in the National Football League is the pressure of it. He does that for a living. So, I don’t think he’d have any problem."

Kane, a longtime Patriots fan, recently became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or, soccer’s award for the best player in the world.

The 33-year-old England captain this month signed a contract extension to stay at Bayern until 2029, so it’s unclear when he’d be ready to give NFL kicking a shot.

Kane has mused over the years about trying it. He has even floated the idea of combining his NFL dream with joining a Major League Soccer team.

"I think I’ve seen him maybe kick a few, and he looked pretty good," Maye said. "No doubt, he does that for a living, so I’m sure he’d be just fine."

Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little weighed in on Kane a few days after booting a game-winning 57-yard field goal to beat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 in London a month ago. Little said Kane's biggest adjustment would be shifting from star striker to bit player. As a kicker, he said, "You’re out there just to back everyone up basically."

Bayern is still celebrating its first Ballon d’Or winner in 45 years. It’s also the first for any player at a German club since 1996.

Patriots tight end Hunter Henry said he doesn't know much about soccer but was well aware of the Bayern star: "He’s a dawg — lot of respect for Harry Kane."

Reporting by The Associated Press.

item.title: Historic vote nixes 150-year booze ban in once-dry New Jersey town
item.description: A New Jersey town has ended its 153-year alcohol ban with 60.4% of voters approving sales, yet residents of the area are divided over the BYOB culture.
item.content:encoded:
A suburb of Philadelphia has voted to end its long-standing ban on alcohol sales — reversing restrictions that date back more than 150 years.

Voters in Collingswood, New Jersey, approved a ballot measure on Nov. 3 allowing alcohol sales at licensed establishments. The move lifts restrictions that have existed in the town since the 19th century.

The ballot question read, "Shall the retail sale of all kinds of alcoholic beverages, for consumption on the licensed premises by the glass or other open receptacle... be permitted in this municipality?"

WINE, BEER OR LIQUOR: STUDY FINDS ONE DRINK IS LINKED TO LOWER RISK OF DEATH THAN OTHERS

Election data obtained by Fox News Digital from Camden County show that 3,635 residents voted in favor of the measure, while 2,381 people voted against it.

The measure passed with roughly 60.4% of the vote, compared with 39.6% opposed, a margin of 1,254 votes.

A total of 6,016 votes were cast on the municipal question, with all 12 precincts reporting.

The town's alcohol restrictions date back to 1873, when residents voted to ban alcohol sales in the area, then part of Haddon Township, according to a 2019 environmental resource inventory published by the Borough of Collingswood.

RED WINE OR WHITE WINE? DOCTOR REVEALS THE HEALTHIER CHOICE, AS WELL AS CAUTIONARY DETAILS

In 1935 — two years after Prohibition ended — Collingswood residents voted against a ballot measure that would have allowed retail alcohol sales and the issuance of liquor licenses.

A total of 3,859 voted against the measure and just 774 in favor, according to a New Jersey Alcoholic Beverage Control bulletin from that year.

Collingswood Deputy Mayor Amy Henderson Riley welcomed the results, calling the vote "historic."

"After 91 years, Collingswood is no longer a dry town," Riley said in a social media post, referring to the 1935 ballot measure. "That's historic."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

A month before the election, Reddit users in a South Jersey-themed forum debated whether Collingswood should lift its longstanding alcohol ban.

"Collingswood is an epicenter of food in South Jersey and deserves a liquor license," one person said.

"The alcohol ban is dumb and people are scared of change," another Redditor wrote.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Others were divided over whether allowing alcohol sales would benefit the borough's restaurant scene.

"I don't know. I like the whole BYOB vibe," a Redditor said. "I'd rather spend my money on good food."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Counterpoint: Collingswood is an epicenter of food in SJ because there are no liquor licenses," another person said. "Restaurants succeed or fail based on the quality of their food and not their ability to finance a license."

The vote came as another centuries-old alcohol restriction faces scrutiny, with the U.S. Supreme Court agreeing to review a federal ban on distilling spirits at home.

The law, which dates back to 1868, prohibits Americans from making whiskey and other distilled spirits at home, even for personal consumption, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

item.title: US attorney and Senate Dem spar in dueling letters demanding records preservation: 'I will not be intimidated'
item.description: Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut responded to a letter issued by U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz, declaring, "I will not be intimidated."
item.content:encoded:
After U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz issued a letter ordering Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., to preserve materials pertaining to the lawmaker's alleged "intent to deny citizens of their core constitutional rights," the senator responded in kind by ordering Reitz to preserve materials pertaining to the decision to issue his letter.

"In recent weeks, you have threatened citizens for associating themselves with the President and other public officials," Reitz claimed in his letter to Blumenthal Wednesday.

A footnote points to an October Blumenthal press release about the senator issuing letters demanding information from individuals and the heads of companies that the Washington Post indicated had committed donations for the construction of President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom project.

"It is also extraordinary for an elected official to intimidate citizens for engaging in philanthropic practices that will benefit our nation for generations. The American people are entitled to freely associate without elected officials terrorizing them with aggressive, harassing government action," Reitz wrote.

TOP DEM ON COMMITTEE FIRES BACK AFTER WHITE HOUSE COUNSEL WARNS AGAINST OVERREACH AMID INVESTIGATION THREATS

"I therefore write to formally give you notice of your obligation to preserve all documents, communications, and other electronically stored information relevant to your intent to deprive citizens of their core constitutional rights in violation of 18 U.S.C. §§ 241 and 242. 

"You are obligated to preserve all potentially relevant evidence related to your efforts to suppress associational activities for philanthropic projects throughout the nation's capital," the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas demanded.

Blumenthal, the ranking member on the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, fired back in a letter to Reitz also dated Nov. 11.

"I am aware of your letter, posted to X today, which purports to initiate an investigation into me for conducting a congressional inquiry. This is just the latest in a series of unlawful actions on the part of the Trump Administration attempting to intimidate Members of Congress for engaging in constitutionally protected activity. Your implied threat of an investigation is baseless," the senator wrote.

'LAWYER UP': DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

"As incoming Chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, I will not be intimidated. I will work on behalf of the American people to vigorously pursue investigations into this Administration’s misuse of taxpayer dollars and any corporate entity that has enabled its boundless corruption," Blumenthal continued.

"The public deserves to know the terms under which dozens of American companies were persuaded to donate millions of dollars to the President’s vanity projects, and whether lawsuits were dismissed, contracts were awarded, or regulations went unenforced in exchange for that money.

"The public deserves transparency about whether the White House and the corporations it cajoled extracted favors at the expense of American taxpayers. Not only are these appropriate subjects for congressional oversight, but such inquiries are among the constitutional duties that Members of Congress must undertake to become informed about matters on which legislation may be necessary."

Then in a tit-for-tat, the senator ordered Reitz to retain all materials related to the decision to issue his letter.

RO KHANNA REJECTS WARNINGS THAT TRUMP ADMIN INVESTIGATIONS COULD DERAIL DEMOCRATS' AFFORDABILITY AGENDA

"Since you appear to have evidence of the Trump Administration’s efforts to protect corporate donors and Administration officials from legitimate oversight, I accordingly direct you to preserve all records and correspondence, including all communications with the White House or senior officials at the Department of Justice, related to the decision to draft and post your letter," Blumenthal wrote.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment Thursday.

item.title: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for plotting murder of lover's husband, offers no last words
item.description: James Pavatt was pronounced dead after lethal injection for plotting the 2001 murder of Rob Andrew, who was gunned down in his garage just before Thanksgiving.
item.content:encoded:
An Oklahoma man convicted of plotting with his lover to kill her estranged husband 25 years ago was executed Thursday without uttering any final words.

James Pavatt, 73, was put to death by lethal injection at the Oklahoma State Penitentiary in McAlester for the 2001 murder of Rob Andrew, a 39-year-old advertising executive who was gunned down in his garage while picking up his two young children just before Thanksgiving.

Pavatt was pronounced dead at 10:12 a.m. local time, according to the Oklahoma Department of Corrections. Prison officials described the execution as "uneventful," adding that Pavatt had no last words, according to local news station KOKH.

FLORIDA DEATH ROW INMATE USES LAST WORDS TO MAINTAIN INNOCENCE BEFORE EXECUTION

For his last meal, Pavatt requested a strawberry milkshake and a barbecue dinner of smoked chicken, brisket, pulled pork, fried okra, baked beans and pickles, KOCO reported.

Pavatt was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. He had been having an affair with Rob Andrew's wife, Brenda Andrew, who was convicted in a separate trial and also sentenced to death.

Weeks before the killing, Rob Andrew told police someone was trying to kill him after the brake lines on his car were cut.

Brenda Andrew later claimed masked intruders shot her in the arm and fatally shot her husband at the Oklahoma City home the couple previously shared. Prosecutors, however, said she and Pavatt plotted the murder.

The pair fled to Mexico with Brenda Andrew's two children after the shooting but were arrested three months later while re-entering the United States.

At a clemency hearing last month, Pavatt maintained his innocence and claimed Brenda Andrew had manipulated him.

ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION

"It was not until my trial that I began to see the extent to which I had been manipulated by Brenda," he told the board. "I can see why the jury believed that we were both involved in Rob's murder."

Prosecutors maintained that both were equally responsible for the killing, regardless of who fired the fatal shots.

Pavatt's execution was the first of two scheduled in the United States on Thursday. In Texas, John Allen Rubio, 46, was set to be executed that evening for the 2003 stabbing and beheading of three young children he was raising in Brownsville. The victims were 3 years old, 14 months old and 2 months old.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: House Dem misses Hegseth impeachment vote because of major medical procedure one week after Election Day
item.description: Democratic Rep. Lou Correa, one of the House members who did not vote Tuesday on the Hegseth impeachment issue, underwent open-heart surgery that day.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Lou Correa, D-Calif. — one of the more than a dozen House members who did not vote Tuesday on the impeachment push against Department of War Secretary Pete Hegseth — explained that he had open-heart surgery.

"Thank you to everyone who has reached out with prayers, well wishes, and words of encouragement. Your kindness means a great deal to my family and me. On Tuesday, November 10th, I underwent emergency open-heart surgery. The surgery went well, and I am now recovering," the congressman said in a Wednesday post on X.

"When medically cleared, I’ll return to Washington, D.C., and continue fighting for Orange County. In the meantime, I’ll continue working from the district alongside my team to serve our constituents. To the doctors, surgeons, nurses, and medical staff: Thank you for the extraordinary care you’ve provided and the compassion you've shown my family. Nos vemos pronto," he added, which translates from Spanish to English as "See you soon."

EL-SAYED TELLS HEGSETH TO RESIGN AFTER IMPEACHMENT EFFORT FAILS: 'MAKE IT EASY FOR EVERYBODY'

Over the weekend, the congressman experienced a heart attack, according to the Orange County Register.

Correa's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on Thursday.

The House voted 211-204 on Tuesday to refer the articles of impeachment to the Judiciary Committee, avoiding a vote on the actual articles of impeachment. Eleven House Democrats and seven House Republicans did not vote.

HEGSETH COULD FACE NEW IMPEACHMENT PUSH OVER UKRAINE AID, LAWMAKERS WARN

Rep. Thomas Massie, the outgoing GOP lawmaker behind the impeachment articles, was the only House Republican who voted against the move to sideline the impeachment effort.

While Correa couldn't be there for the vote, he declared in a Tuesday post on X, "I vehemently support the impeachment of Secretary Hegseth.

HEGSETH THWARTS GOP-LED IMPEACHMENT PUSH AS QUESTIONS SWIRL OVER WHETHER ALLEGATIONS RISE TO HIGH CRIMES

"Hegseth has dragged us into another endless war. He has fired experienced generals who disagree with him and the president. And under his leadership, the military has blatantly discriminated against women, LGBTQ+ service members, and others. Our troops deserve a Secretary of Defense who puts their safety first and honors our Constitution," Correa added.

item.title: Supermodel goes Instagram official with hockey and hot dogs, dating the boss' daughter & don't try this
item.description: Bella Hadid went Instagram official with Nathan Lacy at a Colorado Avalanche game, plus a boss playing matchmaker and a jealous best friend.
item.content:encoded:
This week we're feeling the chill of the ice during a hockey game and housing hot dogs for love. It's not your typical setting for going Instagram official, but it's the one a supermodel chose to take earlier this week.

That sets the mood for this week's edition of True Romance. We're going outside of the traditional box. The boss is trying to hook you up with his daughter, you're not trying to land a date with her.

Also, it's good to trust your gut sometimes. Your best friend could actually be jealous of your "too good to be true" significant other and execute a plan to ruin your happiness. Nobody wants a friend like that.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Let's get back to that supermodel who decided hockey and hot dogs were the perfect formula for hard launch. It's Bella Hadid and, according to Page Six, the new man in her life is Nathan Lacy.

The two were rinkside at a Colorado Avalanche game over the weekend "Honoring Hockey Fights Cancer." It was in an Instagram post about being at the game where Lacy showed up and, by the rules of society, became official.

Hockey and hot dogs. Is there a more romantic setting than that? There are a few that are on the same level, but I can't think of any that top it.

Congratulations to the lovely couple and to the Avalanche for landing a supermodel as a new fan. Hockey is alive and well.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook and keep sending your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

It isn’t often that your boss is the one trying to set you up with his daughter. That, to me, is a sign that there's something else at work here.

Is it fate? Are you the one that's supposed to teach your boss that it's not a great idea to set one of his employees up with his daughter?

You'll never know by sitting on the sideline overthinking the situation. There could be other employees he has in mind, and you could miss out on something special.

That's where this 23-year-old finds himself. He's on Reddit wasting his time asking, "What do you guys think I should do?"

He's conflicted about how to proceed. He finds it strange that his boss is trying to set him up with his daughter, instead of what it really is. And that's a sign.

JOE BURROW'S GIRLFRIEND SHARES CHEATING HOT TAKE, WOMAN'S SISTER HOOKED UP WITH HER DATE & REGAINING THE SPARK

Not just any sign. A sign from the universe. Here's how he said it all came together and how his boss approached him about dating the 21-year-old daughter:

"I was working with 2 of my co workers out for a job today and at around 4:30 we were waiting for our boss to come and pick us up. When he came to pick us up, he told me that he wants me to date her," the employee wrote.

"He even called her while we were there and had me talk to her. Once we got to his house to drop off the gear, I was sitting and talking with her for a bit."

The hard part is out of the way. The dad approves and you've already met her.

"I am a bit conflicted on what to do. On 1 hand, its strange that my boss would try to set me up with his daughter even though Ive only been working with him for around a month now," he continued.

"On the other hand, she looks really pretty and I would not mind dating her at all."

Let’s throw a third hand into the mix for fun. Why not? This guy could use all the help he can get.

What's the worst thing that could happen? Now, throw that out because that scenario will never happen.

What are you left with? A shot at love and job security. Isn't that enough?

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook.

This next one is a cautionary tale about trusting your gut. She, for 10 months, dated a guy that she thought was Mr. Right.

The sad reality is that he could have been. She'll never know after her best friend, who she suspected was jealous of what she had, ruined it for her.

"I really thought I’d found my Mr Right; a lovely guy who had all the same interests, and the sex was out of this world. So the truth about him has completely floored me, and I just can’t seem to pick myself up," the heartbroken woman wrote to Metro.

"My best friend was always skeptical about him, which I’ll be honest, I put down to jealousy. She just kept telling me he seemed too good to be true, and she turned out to be right."

Or was she? Was she right or did she ruin it all for you on purpose? Those are two very different things. Let's see where it goes from here.

Her best friend did some snooping behind her back and found out that he was married with two small children. She knew nothing about his family.

"Unbeknown to me, she did a bit of social media digging, which ended up with her getting in touch with the guy’s wife to double check whether her suspicions were right," she said.

"She worried that the wife would go mad but instead she was very civil. She said it wasn’t the first time he’d cheated, and that if she didn’t have little children she’d have kicked him out long ago."

It all made sense to her now. The reason she had never been invited back to his place and the annoying roommate that turned out to be his wife suddenly snapped into focus.

She broke up with him, instead of doing what she should have done and ended her friendship with her best friend. Without the best friend and her toxic jealousy, she would still be with Mr. Right.

It's clear her best friend didn’t want to see her happy. If he could hide a secret family from her for 10 months, he could certainly have forever.

These supposed "cringe things" are exactly why so many men and women have a hard time communicating. A man leaving his wife just to ask you out on a date is what used to be called romance.

Being called a man's "big red tractor" isn't cringe. It's him pouring his heart and soul out to you. Thigh-warmed pocket tacos are a token of love if you ask any mature adult who isn’t thinking only about themselves.

Call these cringe if you want, and sure some might be, but don't you dare tell me that all of these are cringe. Asking you to sign an Instagram photo for his wall is the guy at the gym's attempt to break the ice.

-------------

That's it. Another week in the books. Keep the song of the week suggestions coming and any tales of romance you wish to share.

You can reach me, anonymously if you prefer, at sean.joseph@outkick.com. Also, go follow along on Twitter and Facebook.

item.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: DA identifies 49 local killers slated for Newsom's death row clemency — and their crimes

MICHAEL RUIZ: CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS REVOLT AFTER NEWSOM ORDERS STATE'S WORST KILLERS OFF DEATH ROW

Deleon is a former child actor, born John Jacobson Jr. and was separately convicted of the 2003 murder of an associate named Jon Jarvi from Anaheim.

item.title: Trump asks Vance to focus on ‘corruption and crime’ in Dem-run cities, states
item.description: President Trump says JD Vance will target alleged corruption in Minnesota, California and Illinois, claiming billions are stolen monthly from government programs.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Thursday that he has asked Vice President JD Vance to focus his "complete and total attention" on alleged widespread corruption and crime in Democrat-led cities and states, accusing blue state leaders of allowing billions of dollars to be stolen each month.

In a Truth Social post, Trump singled out Minnesota, California and Illinois as examples of states he claims are plagued by corruption and mismanagement, arguing that cracking down on the alleged criminal activity could help balance the federal budget.

"I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.," Trump wrote.

JD VANCE WARNS BLUE STATE OFFICIALS COULD FACE PRISON OVER BILLION-DOLLAR FRAUD EPIDEMIC

"The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters," he continued. "Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month."

Trump did not provide specific examples in his post of how billions of dollars are allegedly being stolen each month.

Vance already leads the White House's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, which Trump established through a March 16 executive order aimed at combating fraud, waste and abuse in federally funded benefit programs.

The task force is charged with coordinating federal efforts to strengthen eligibility verification, prevent improper payments and identify suspected fraud in government benefit programs.

WALZ ADMINISTRATION IGNORED FRAUD WARNINGS AS BILLIONS VANISHED, HOUSE OVERSIGHT REPORT ALLEGES

The executive order also identified Minnesota, California and Illinois among states where the administration alleged widespread fraud or vulnerabilities in government benefit programs.

In October, Fox News Digital reported that the Vance-led task force was preparing to announce criminal charges against more than 40 defendants in an alleged $40 million Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme.

At the time, the task force reported identifying $260.7 billion in suspected fraud since Trump took office and preventing an estimated $72 billion in potentially fraudulent payments on an annualized basis. Those figures have not been independently verified.

It was not immediately clear whether Trump's latest directive would expand Vance's existing responsibilities or signal a renewed emphasis on investigating alleged corruption in Democratic-led jurisdictions.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Department of Justice for comment on the president's directive and the allegations of widespread fraud.

Trump also suggested that eliminating the alleged corruption could help balance the federal budget.

VANCE-LED TASK FORCE CUTS OFF $1.4B FROM HOME HEALTH, HOSPICE PROVIDERS SUSPECTED OF FRAUD

"Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity," Trump wrote, before adding, "CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood!"

The president did not explain how eliminating the alleged corruption would balance the federal budget.

Trump then pivoted to Iran, declaring that the United States no longer needs to negotiate a deal with Tehran.

"We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote. "We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!"

Trump did not elaborate on his claims regarding Iranian funds or the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically important waterway for global energy shipments.

Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for clarification on the president's remarks regarding Iran.

item.title: Howard Lutnick is next Trump official top Dems want on the chopping block amid NVIDIA scandal
item.description: Top House Democrats are calling for an investigation into Howard Lutnick over his alleged role in the NVIDIA Jensen Huang Chinese spy scandal.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE : Top House Democrats are calling for an investigation into Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over allegations involving NVIDIA's former CEO's reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigned this week following allegations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

In the midst of the spy scandal, multiple investigative reports emerged claiming Lutnick received a classified memo warning him about Huang’s relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, of no familial relation to the NVIDIA CEO.

"Howard Lutnick needs to be investigated over his role in Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy, we're going to have an investigation into those allegations, that's completely unacceptable," Rep. Ted Lieu, D-Calif., who is expected to become chairman of the House Democratic Caucus, told Fox News Digital.

FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL

Lieu alleged that despite Lutnick being briefed on the reported relationship between Huang and a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy, he failed to take action.

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., a vice chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and member of the House Select Committee on China, also expressed support for investigating Lutnick and did not rule out examining Secretary of State Marco Rubio's involvement, as well.

"I think we need transparency," Khanna told Fox News Digital. "I think we need to understand what they knew."

PROGRESSIVE GROUP'S 182-PAGE BLUEPRINT MAPS OUT POTENTIAL DEM INVESTIGATIONS INTO TRUMP, CORPORATE ALLIES

"Rubio knew about the Chinese spy, and then got invited to the China trip," Khanna continued. "We need to get to the bottom of this."

Lutnick and Rubio did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

REBECCA GRANT: JENSEN HUANG OWES AMERICA AN APOLOGY, AND NVIDIA OWES INVESTORS ANSWERS

Many left-leaning lawmakers are jumping on the chance to name the Cabinet official they want to see face scrutiny when Democrats take back control of the House in January.

However, neither Khanna or Lieu shed light on how they would investigate, prosecute or remove Lutnick, and potentially Rubio. Neither of the Cabinet secretaries has been formally accused or indicted of wrongdoing in connection with the NVIDIA case.

House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is currently running unopposed for the Democratic nomination for Speaker of the House, did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on whether he spoke to either lawmakers on their desires to take action against Lutnick and Rubio.

HAKEEM JEFFRIES DECLARES BID FOR HOUSE SPEAKER AFTER GOP'S MIDTERM MASSACRE

The lawmakers' remarks signal that congressional Democrats could use their incoming majority to investigate senior Trump administration officials over their handling of alleged Chinese intelligence threats.

It is unclear whether Republican lawmakers will support the Democrats' investigations. But following Huang’s resignation, House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., announced that the outgoing CEO has agreed to brief congressional committees following the scandal.

He also advocated for Congress to act quickly to pass bipartisan export control legislation in the year-end national defense bill.

Moolenaar welcomed the resignation and added that companies such as NVIDIA should "never jeopardize our nation’s security by giving Chinese companies access to their most advanced chips," and called on them to "change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority."
